title: Java for Android Interviews
description: Java semantics, collections, concurrency, Android lifecycle, and production reliability.

courses.title: Java for Android Interviews
courses.description: Java semantics, collections, concurrency, Android lifecycle, and production reliability.

chapters.title: 1 · Core Java
chapters.summary: Reason about equality, immutability, generics, and exceptions.

lessons.title: Values and equality
lessons.explanation: Trace Java behavior beyond surface syntax.

exercises.prompt: Two strings have the same characters but may be different objects. Which comparison checks content?
exercises.code:
String a = new String("ok");
String b = new String("ok");
exercises.explanation: equals compares String content; == compares references. Matching hashes alone do not prove equality.

exercises.prompt: What is the safe way to compare two nullable Integer values by numeric value?
options: left == right for every boxed value
exercises.explanation: Objects.equals handles null and value equality without relying on reference caching or unboxing null.

exercises.prompt: A class overrides equals by transaction ID but not hashCode. What can fail?
options: The compiler rejects every class instance
HashMap and HashSet lookup or deduplication
exercises.explanation: Equal objects must produce equal hashes; hash collections use both methods.

exercises.prompt: A mutable key changes a field used by hashCode after insertion. What is a likely symptom?
options: The same key may no longer be found in its original hash bucket
exercises.explanation: Mutating hash-relevant state breaks the bucket invariant. Prefer immutable keys.

exercises.prompt: A final List reference points to an ArrayList. What does final prevent?
options: Reassigning the reference, not mutating the list
Other aliases from changing the list
exercises.explanation: final applies to the variable binding. Wrap or copy the collection for stronger immutability.

exercises.prompt: Two overloads accept String and Integer. What happens when calling method(null) with no cast?
exercises.explanation: Neither parameter type is more specific than the other, so overload resolution cannot choose.

exercises.prompt: A parser receives malformed external text. Which design makes failure explicit to callers?
options: Use a null pointer to signal failure
Print a stack trace and continue as success
Return a result or throw a documented parsing exception with context
Catch Exception and return an unrelated valid value
exercises.explanation: A clear failure contract lets callers reject invalid records or report the offending row.

exercises.prompt: Fill the value comparison safe for nullable boxed integers.
exercises.explanation: Objects.equals handles null and invokes value equality for non-null values.

lessons.title: Types and contracts
lessons.explanation: Avoid unsafe variance and hidden mutation.

exercises.prompt: Why cannot List<Dog> be passed where List<Animal> is expected?
options: Generics are always covariant at runtime
Java generics are invariant; List<Animal> could accept a Cat
exercises.explanation: Invariant generic types protect writes. Use a bounded wildcard for read-only consumption.

exercises.prompt: A method only reads Animal values from a list. Which parameter accepts List<Dog>?
options: List<? super Dog> when reading Animal safely
exercises.explanation: An extends wildcard is a producer of Animal values; it does not permit adding arbitrary Animals.

exercises.prompt: A method inserts Dog values into a caller-supplied list. Which parameter permits List<Dog> and List<Animal>?
exercises.explanation: A super wildcard is a consumer of Dog; reads return Object unless narrowed.

exercises.prompt: A final class stores a mutable Date passed to its constructor and returns it from a getter. Why is it not immutable?
options: Callers can mutate the same Date through aliases
exercises.explanation: Defensive copies or immutable value types are needed at both ingress and egress.

exercises.prompt: A subclass adds a new field to equality while its parent equality ignores it. What risk arises?
options: Symmetry or transitivity can break across parent and child comparisons
The JVM automatically compares all fields
exercises.explanation: Equality across inheritance is subtle; value objects are often safer as final classes.

exercises.prompt: A file stream must close if parsing throws. Which construct expresses the lifetime?
exercises.explanation: try-with-resources closes AutoCloseable values on normal and exceptional exits.

exercises.prompt: A method declares throws IOException. What must a caller generally do?
options: Ignore it because all exceptions are unchecked
Catch it or declare it in its own signature
exercises.explanation: Checked exceptions are enforced by the compiler at call sites.

exercises.prompt: Fill the read-only producer bound for animal subtypes.
exercises.explanation: extends allows reading subtype values as Animal without permitting unsafe insertion.

chapters.title: 2 · Collections and algorithms
chapters.summary: Choose structures and verify complexity and boundaries.

lessons.title: Maps, sets, and heaps
lessons.explanation: Make large input handling efficient and correct.

exercises.prompt: A million event IDs must be deduplicated in arrival order. Which expected O(n) strategy works?
options: Track HashSet membership while appending unseen IDs to an ArrayList
Sort first and return that order
Compare each pair with nested loops
exercises.explanation: A set supports expected constant-time membership; the output list preserves first appearance.

exercises.prompt: Count transaction types. Which update handles a missing key?
exercises.explanation: merge initializes an absent count to 1 and adds for an existing count.

exercises.prompt: A payment log has repeated event IDs. Complete a frequency map that retains all counts.
exercises.hiddenTests: For [a,b,a], return {a:2,b:1}; empty input returns an empty map.

guided.explanation: HashMap stores one counter per ID. merge initializes the first occurrence and adds later ones.

exercises.explanation: HashMap stores one counter per ID. merge initializes the first occurrence and adds later ones.

exercises.prompt: Keep the largest 100 values from a stream of one million using limited memory. Which structure fits?
options: A HashSet with no size bound
An ArrayList of all values then sort
exercises.explanation: A min-heap keeps the current threshold at its head with O(n log k) time and O(k) space.

exercises.prompt: Remove matching entries while iterating an ArrayList with an Iterator. Which action is safe?
options: Call list.remove(value) during the same iteration
Replace the list reference with null
exercises.explanation: Iterator.remove follows the iterator modification protocol; direct structural changes can cause ConcurrentModificationException.

exercises.prompt: A comparator returns a.score - b.score for arbitrary int scores. What bug can occur?
options: Subtraction can overflow and violate comparator ordering
Scores are automatically widened to long
exercises.explanation: Integer.compare(a.score, b.score) avoids overflow and preserves comparator consistency.

exercises.prompt: A PriorityQueue is iterated directly. Can that traversal be assumed sorted?
options: Yes; iterator always yields sorted order
It is sorted by insertion time
No; only head removal follows priority order
exercises.explanation: The heap invariant governs peek/poll, not iterator traversal order.

exercises.prompt: Fill the queue operation that removes the smallest head of a min-heap.
exercises.explanation: poll removes the head, keeping only the largest k values. peek would read without shrinking the heap.

lessons.title: Search and windows
lessons.explanation: State invariants that justify each pointer move.

exercises.prompt: A sorted array must yield two numbers summing to target. What is the O(n) approach?
options: Move both pointers on every step
Start at both ends and move the side that changes the sum toward target
exercises.explanation: Sorted order proves that moving the low pointer raises the sum and moving the high pointer lowers it.

exercises.prompt: Why does a standard grow/shrink sum window fail with negative numbers?
options: Removing a negative can increase the sum
exercises.explanation: The monotonic sum argument requires nonnegative values; use a different technique for signed input.

exercises.prompt: Count subarrays summing to k with signed values. Which prefix map entry must be seeded?
exercises.explanation: The empty prefix represents subarrays beginning at index zero.

exercises.prompt: A binary search computes mid = (low + high) / 2 for very large nonnegative indices. What is safer?
exercises.explanation: The safer form avoids overflow in low + high while keeping the same midpoint.

exercises.prompt: Find first value >= x. If a[mid] qualifies, what happens to the upper bound?
options: Return immediately even if earlier values qualify
Set high = mid so mid remains a candidate
exercises.explanation: Lower bound keeps a qualifying mid while searching for an earlier one.

exercises.prompt: Recursive DFS follows a chain of 200,000 nodes. What non-time complexity risk appears?
options: Only the number of edges doubles
exercises.explanation: A deep chain uses one call frame per node; an explicit stack can avoid call-stack exhaustion.

exercises.prompt: Window sums of int amounts may overflow. What should the accumulator use?
options: long, converting before addition where needed
int because each element is int
exercises.explanation: The aggregate range can exceed each element range; long prevents common int overflow cases.

exercises.prompt: Fill the initial prefix frequency for subarrays that begin at zero.
exercises.template:
Map<Long, Integer> counts = new HashMap<>();
counts.put(____1);
exercises.explanation: The empty prefix sum zero appears once before reading any element.

chapters.title: 3 · Concurrency and JVM behavior
chapters.summary: Protect shared state and task lifetime.

lessons.title: Visibility and atomicity
lessons.explanation: Distinguish seeing a value from updating it safely.

exercises.prompt: A worker polls a stop flag written by another thread. What does volatile provide?
options: Visibility of writes and reads of the flag
exercises.explanation: volatile gives visibility and ordering guarantees for the field; it does not make compound updates atomic.

exercises.prompt: Two threads each execute count++ 10,000 times on a volatile int. Why may the result be less than 20,000?
options: int cannot be shared between threads
Increment is read-modify-write, not one atomic operation
exercises.explanation: Both threads can read the same old value and overwrite one increment.

exercises.prompt: Which type supports atomic increment without a synchronized block?
exercises.explanation: AtomicInteger implements the update atomically, avoiding lost increments.

exercises.prompt: Thread A holds lock X then wants Y; B holds Y then wants X. What is the failure mode?
exercises.explanation: Circular wait prevents either thread from progressing. Consistent lock order can prevent it.

exercises.prompt: A HashMap is mutated concurrently without coordination. What is a sound replacement when independent operations need thread safety?
options: ConcurrentHashMap, while still designing multi-step atomicity separately
volatile HashMap reference with same unsynchronized mutations
exercises.explanation: ConcurrentHashMap supports concurrent basic operations; compound invariants still need compute or other coordination.

exercises.prompt: Two threads update one map counter using get then put. Which operation can make that per-key update atomic?
exercises.explanation: compute applies a remapping operation atomically for a key; separate get/put can lose updates.

exercises.prompt: A thread reads a field after another thread writes it with no synchronization. What can be assumed?
options: The JVM automatically locks every read
No guaranteed visibility or ordering for that data race
The latest write is always visible
exercises.explanation: The Java memory model requires a happens-before relationship for reliable cross-thread observation.

exercises.prompt: Fill the atomic counter operation.
exercises.template:
AtomicInteger count = new AtomicInteger();
int next = count.____1();
exercises.explanation: incrementAndGet performs a single atomic increment and returns the new value.

lessons.title: Executors and cancellation
lessons.explanation: Bound work and clean up tasks explicitly.

exercises.prompt: An Android screen creates an ExecutorService for requests. What should happen when its owner ends?
options: Cancel or transfer owned tasks and shut down an owned executor appropriately
exercises.explanation: Task and executor ownership must be explicit to avoid work outliving the feature.

exercises.prompt: What does Future.cancel(true) request?
options: Interruption of a running task, which must cooperate
Guaranteed immediate termination of every operation
Deletion of all task results from disk
exercises.explanation: Interruption is cooperative; blocking operations and code must handle it appropriately.

exercises.prompt: A blocking worker catches InterruptedException and cannot complete. What is a good default?
options: Convert it to a successful result
Stop work or restore interrupt status when propagating through an API that cannot throw it
exercises.explanation: Interruption is a cancellation signal. Swallowing it can keep canceled work alive.

exercises.prompt: A network feature submits unlimited tasks to an unbounded queue. What production risk appears?
options: The JVM rejects every new task immediately
Backlog and memory growth under sustained load
exercises.explanation: Concurrency and queue limits are resource policies; unbounded work can exhaust memory.

exercises.prompt: A button handler performs synchronous network I/O on Android main thread. What should be changed?
options: Wrap the call in synchronized on the UI view
Move I/O to owned background work and post state changes to main
exercises.explanation: Blocking the main thread freezes input and rendering and can trigger ANR.

exercises.prompt: Search A starts, then B; A completes last. How can a Java UI reject A?
options: Track a request generation or cancel A, checking before UI application
exercises.explanation: Response order differs from user intent; compare results with the current query.

exercises.prompt: Why are immutable DTO snapshots useful between worker and UI threads?
options: They automatically replace the need for main-thread UI rules
They avoid shared mutable aliases and simplify visibility reasoning at the handoff
exercises.explanation: Owned immutable values reduce data races; the handoff mechanism still matters.

exercises.prompt: Fill the method used to restore interrupt status after catching InterruptedException.
exercises.explanation: Restoring the interrupt flag lets upstream code observe the cancellation signal.

chapters.title: 4 · Android with Java
chapters.summary: Apply lifecycle, background work, and interoperability safely.

lessons.title: Lifecycle and UI
lessons.explanation: Keep screen state and work tied to the right owner.

exercises.prompt: An Activity recreates during rotation. Where should ongoing screen data normally live?
options: A ViewModel or repository, with durable data persisted separately
exercises.explanation: The Activity instance is recreated; a ViewModel retains screen state across configuration changes.

exercises.prompt: A ViewModel holds an unsent edit. The process dies. What must have happened for the edit to survive?
options: It was committed to durable local storage
exercises.explanation: ViewModels do not survive process death. Durable edits require persistence.

exercises.prompt: RecyclerView rows reorder after refresh. What helps keep item-specific UI state matched?
options: Stable domain IDs with correct DiffUtil identity comparison
exercises.explanation: Item IDs describe identity across reorder; positions are transient.

exercises.prompt: A recycled ViewHolder receives an image from its prior item request. What should binding do?
options: Store the image in a global static field
Cancel or validate the old request against the current item ID
Assume the old request finishes first
exercises.explanation: Recycling reuses views, so a late callback must verify it still belongs to the bound item.

exercises.prompt: A singleton stores an Activity Context. What can happen?
options: The destroyed Activity remains reachable and leaks
exercises.explanation: Long-lived objects should not retain short-lived Activity instances; use an appropriate application context.

exercises.prompt: A Java API has no nullability annotations and Kotlin calls it. What danger appears?
options: Kotlin sees a platform type and may assume non-null incorrectly
exercises.explanation: Annotating Java contracts and checking at boundaries reduces platform-type null hazards.

exercises.prompt: A location permission is denied. What should the feature do?
options: Render a clear denied path and offer a contextual retry or alternative
Crash on the first null location
exercises.explanation: Permission denial is a normal user choice and needs an explicit UI state.

exercises.prompt: Fill the Activity method used to post a small view update to the main thread.
exercises.explanation: Android views should be updated on the main thread.

lessons.title: Persistence and jobs
lessons.explanation: Use durable data and bounded Android work.

exercises.prompt: A screen must show cached feed rows offline. What should it observe?
options: A fetch inside every row bind
Room-backed local data; network refresh writes updates to Room
exercises.explanation: Local storage provides an offline source of truth while sync updates it.

exercises.prompt: An order header and items must persist together. What prevents half-written orders?
options: A database transaction around both writes
A delay after the first insert
exercises.explanation: A transaction commits or rolls back the related writes as one unit.

exercises.prompt: A deferrable upload must run after process death when network returns. What Android API fits?
options: A thread started from a destroyed Activity
exercises.explanation: WorkManager persists scheduled deferrable work and can wait for connectivity.

exercises.prompt: A Retrofit call receives HTTP 500. Which states should the repository distinguish?
options: Every exception as a permission denial
HTTP failure from transport failure and malformed success payload
exercises.explanation: Distinct failure categories support correct retry and debugging decisions.

exercises.prompt: An app update adds a non-null database column. What is required for existing users?
options: A migration or deliberate documented destructive strategy
exercises.explanation: Existing rows and schema need a migration path; entity code alone does not transform stored data.

exercises.prompt: A WorkManager job retries after a timeout; the server may have already applied a payment. What is needed?
options: A stable idempotency key attached to the logical operation
A new random key per retry
exercises.explanation: A stable operation ID lets the server deduplicate repeated delivery.

exercises.prompt: A modern Java language syntax feature compiles locally but fails on an older Android target. What should be checked?
options: Whether the class name is short
Android toolchain desugaring support and device API availability separately
exercises.explanation: Language desugaring and platform APIs are distinct compatibility questions for Android builds.

exercises.prompt: Fill the WorkManager constraint that waits for connectivity.
exercises.explanation: CONNECTED runs the deferrable work only when network is available.

chapters.title: 5 · Real-world Java scenarios
chapters.summary: Handle duplicate events, parsing, payments, and recovery.

lessons.title: Parsing and caches
lessons.explanation: Make failures and capacity rules explicit.

exercises.prompt: A CSV parser splits lines with String.split(",") but fields may contain quoted commas. What is wrong?
options: A comma inside quotes is not a field separator
exercises.explanation: CSV quoting requires a parser aware of quote and escape rules; naive splitting corrupts records.

exercises.prompt: Amounts are decimal currency values. Which representation avoids binary floating-point rounding?
options: double for every exact money operation
Integer minor units or BigDecimal with an explicit scale policy
exercises.explanation: Exact decimal or minor-unit arithmetic avoids binary representation surprises.

exercises.prompt: A bounded in-memory cache evicts the least recently used item. Which Java collection can support this with access ordering?
options: LinkedHashMap configured for access order with eviction policy
exercises.explanation: Access-ordered LinkedHashMap tracks recent use; thread safety requires separate coordination if shared.

exercises.prompt: Multiple threads access a LinkedHashMap LRU cache and mutate access order. What is required?
options: No action because get is always read-only
Synchronization or a proven concurrent cache implementation
Only a volatile reference to the map
exercises.explanation: Access-ordered get mutates ordering; unsynchronized concurrent use is unsafe.

exercises.prompt: A numeric field may exceed long range. What should parsing do?
options: Catch or represent overflow as invalid input with row context
Wrap into a negative value silently
Convert through double and assume exactness
exercises.explanation: Overflow is malformed data for a bounded integer contract; report it explicitly.

exercises.prompt: A parser opens a BufferedReader for each file and occasionally throws. What pattern prevents leaks?
options: Hold every reader in a static list
exercises.explanation: try-with-resources closes on both success and exceptions.

exercises.prompt: A cache uses System.currentTimeMillis for expiry and the wall clock changes. What clock suits elapsed TTL checks?
options: A new random number on each read
A monotonic elapsed-time clock for in-process TTL comparisons
exercises.explanation: Elapsed time should not jump with wall-clock changes; durable expiry across restarts needs a separate policy.

exercises.prompt: Fill the exact arithmetic type for a decimal amount parsed from text.
exercises.explanation: BigDecimal constructed from the decimal string preserves the stated decimal value.

lessons.title: Reliable event processing
lessons.explanation: Settle effects exactly once despite retries and unknown outcomes.

exercises.prompt: The same payment event may be delivered twice. What prevents two balance updates?
options: Atomically record event ID and apply the effect in one transaction
exercises.explanation: Deduplication must be durable and atomic with the effect; a check outside the transaction can race.

exercises.prompt: A payment POST times out after request bytes were sent. What is its correct client state?
options: Unknown until reconciled by stable operation ID
exercises.explanation: The response may be lost after commit; a timeout is not evidence of rollback.

exercises.prompt: An outage causes thousands of clients to retry. Which policy spreads demand?
options: Capped exponential backoff with jitter for safe requests
exercises.explanation: Jitter spreads synchronized clients and a cap bounds resource use.

exercises.prompt: An event fails validation on every retry because required data is missing. What should the worker do?
options: Move it to a dead-letter or explicit failure state with diagnostics
exercises.explanation: Permanent failures need a bounded terminal path so the queue can progress and operators can investigate.

exercises.prompt: A connection receives Connected callback after a newer Disconnect command. What prevents stale state?
options: Check a connection generation/session ID before applying callbacks
Use one global Boolean without ownership
exercises.explanation: Generation tokens reject callbacks from superseded connection attempts.

exercises.prompt: A production payment parser throws. What should a diagnostic record contain?
options: A correlation ID and sanitized error category
exercises.explanation: Sanitized context lets engineers trace failures without exposing sensitive data.

exercises.prompt: Fill the same logical ID on every retry of a charge.
exercises.explanation: A stable idempotency key connects repeated delivery to one charge command.

exercises.prompt: Build a safe payment command pipeline
exercises.story: A mobile checkout queues a charge while offline. A worker can restart and the server response can be lost. Complete each stage.

parts.prompt: Persist a stable command before work is scheduled.
parts.hiddenTests: One order yields one durable command keyed by its stable ID before a job is scheduled.

guided.explanation: Use the order ID, insert the command, then schedule its delivery.

parts.expected: Use the order ID, insert the command, then schedule its delivery.

parts.hiddenTests: Confirmed receipt completes once; uncertain receipt retains same-key command for retry.

guided.explanation: Charge using the stable ID, complete only confirmed work, and retry uncertain outcomes.

parts.expected: Charge using the stable ID, complete only confirmed work, and retry uncertain outcomes.
